patient.name: David Kowalski
patient.chiefComplaint: Crushing substernal chest pain radiating to left arm and jaw

history.hpi: Sudden onset of severe substernal chest pressure approximately 45 minutes ago while resting in his recliner watching TV. Pain radiates to the left arm and jaw, rated 9/10, associated with diaphoresis and nausea. Denies exertion at onset. Denies use of sildenafil, tadalafil, or vardenafil.
history.lastOralIntake: Dinner approximately 3 hours prior to symptom onset
history.events: Wife called 911 after he became pale, diaphoretic, and reported chest pain that would not resolve after sitting down to rest

scene.location: Single-family home, living room, patient seated in a recliner
scene.bystanders: Wife present, called 911 immediately, no CPR performed prior to arrival
visualCues: Patient clutching chest with a fist (Levine's sign)

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 60-year-old male seated in a recliner, pale and diaphoretic, clutching his chest. He reports crushing chest pain radiating to his left arm and jaw for the past 45 minutes.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, speaking full sentences with some effort
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, strong but rapid
otherFindings: Clutching chest with a fist (Levine's sign)
Pain radiates to left arm and jaw, 9/10
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It feels like an elephant is sitting on my chest... it won't go away."

transitions.condition: Crew rapidly performs a 12-lead EKG, administers chewable aspirin, establishes IV access, and transmits a STEMI alert.

phases.name: 12-lead, ASA, and IV started
phases.description: 12-lead EKG confirms an inferior STEMI. Aspirin is given, IV access established, and defibrillator pads placed proactively given the risk of malignant dysrhythmia. STEMI alert transmitted to the receiving facility.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew rapidly performs a 12-lead EKG revealing inferior ST-elevation with reciprocal changes, gives chewable aspirin, establishes IV access, and proactively places defibrillator pads given the risk of a malignant dysrhythmia in this ACS presentation.

otherFindings: STEMI alert transmitted to receiving facility
Denies PDE5 inhibitor use — nitroglycerin candidate
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "The pain's a little better, but it's still there."

expectedActions.shortAction: Acquire 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes of patient contact
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: It is imperative that EMS clinicians routinely acquire a 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes for all patients exhibiting signs and symptoms of ACS
expectedActions.rationale: Early STEMI identification drives time-critical hospital activation.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer aspirin; chewable, non-enteric-coated aspirin preferred (162–325 mg)
expectedActions.rationale: Chewed ASA achieves faster antiplatelet effect in acute MI.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.rationale: Vascular access needed for medications and potential deterioration.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Transmit STEMI alert with advance notification to receiving facility
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Advance notification should be provided to the receiving hospital for patients identified as having a STEMI
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Place defibrillator pads proactively given dysrhythmia risk
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Consider placing defibrillator pads on high-risk patients
expectedActions.rationale: Pre-placed pads eliminate delay if a malignant rhythm develops.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL (SBP >100, no PDE5 use in 48h); may repeat q3–5min
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg sublingual (SL), can repeat q 3–5 minutes if SBP greater than 100 mmHg. The use of nitrates should be avoided in any patient who has used a phosphodiesterase inhibitor within the past 48 hours
expectedActions.rationale: SBP and PDE5 history support safe nitrate administration for ongoing pain.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

transitions.condition: Because defibrillator pads were already placed and rhythm is continuously monitored, when a brief run of nonsustained monomorphic VT occurs it is recognized immediately and the crew is ready to intervene without delay.
Without pads pre-placed, when a run of VT develops and progresses toward sustained VT, the crew must interrupt care to attach pads and charge the defibrillator, delaying definitive treatment.

phases.name: Nonsustained VT self-terminates
phases.description: A brief run of nonsustained VT occurs and self-terminates. The patient remains alert with a palpable pulse throughout. Crew captures the rhythm strip, reassesses pulse and mentation continuously, repeats a 12-lead, and continues STEMI transport.
phases.triggerCondition: With pads already in place and continuous rhythm monitoring, the crew immediately recognizes a 12-beat run of nonsustained monomorphic VT. The patient remains conscious with a palpable pulse throughout, and the run self-terminates after several seconds.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, strong, maintained throughout the rhythm change
otherFindings: Brief run of wide-complex tachycardia self-terminated on the monitor
Pulse and mentation maintained throughout the run
Repeat 12-lead again shows inferior STEMI, unchanged
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I felt a flutter in my chest for a second there."

expectedActions.shortAction: Continuously reassess pulse and mental status during any rhythm change
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Observe for signs of clinical deterioration: dysrhythmias, chest pain, shortness of breath, decreased level of consciousness/syncope, or other signs of shock/hypotension
expectedActions.rationale: Pulse/mentation status determines whether a VT run needs immediate intervention.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform a repeat 12-lead EKG after the rhythm change resolves
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Perform serial 12-lead EKGs (especially if clinical changes are noted)
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms ongoing STEMI pattern and rules out new ischemic change from the VT run.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Keep defibrillator charged/ready for synchronized cardioversion if VT recurs and sustains
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Deliver a synchronized shock based on manufacturer's recommendations
expectedActions.rationale: Readiness minimizes time-to-shock if the next VT run does not self-terminate.

phases.name: Defib pads not placed
phases.description: A run of VT develops unexpectedly. The crew must interrupt care to attach pads. The rhythm fails to terminate and accelerates, and the patient becomes lightheaded with a weak, thready pulse.
phases.triggerCondition: Without defibrillator pads pre-placed, a run of monomorphic VT begins. Because monitoring readiness was not established in advance, precious seconds are lost placing pads and confirming the rhythm while the patient's condition begins to deteriorate.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact but patient increasingly lethargic
otherFindings: Sustained wide-complex tachycardia on the monitor

expectedActions.shortAction: Immediately attach pads and perform synchronized cardioversion for unstable VT
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Regular Wide Complex Tachycardia – Unstable: Deliver a synchronized shock based on manufacturer's recommendation
expectedActions.rationale: Hypotension and altered mentation with sustained VT meet criteria for immediate cardioversion.

expectedActions.shortAction: Consider sedation and analgesia for the responsive patient before cardioversion
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: For responsive patients, consider sedation and analgesia
expectedActions.rationale: Synchronized cardioversion is painful; sedation is appropriate while the patient remains responsive.

transitions.condition: If synchronized cardioversion is not delivered promptly and the patient loses their pulse while still in VT, immediate transition to pulseless cardiac arrest management is required.

phases.name: Pulseless VT — cardiac arrest
phases.description: The patient becomes unresponsive and pulseless while still in monomorphic VT. Crew immediately begins high-quality CPR and treats per the shockable cardiac arrest pathway with defibrillation and epinephrine.
phases.triggerCondition: Cardioversion is not delivered before the patient loses their pulse; the rhythm remains monomorphic VT but the patient is now unresponsive and pulseless, meeting criteria for cardiac arrest.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Absent spontaneous respirations, BVM ventilation initiated
otherFindings: No pulse on palpation — cardiac arrest confirmed

expectedActions.shortAction: Initiate high-quality chest compressions immediately (rate 100–120/min, depth 5–6 cm)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: A rate of greater than 100 and less than 120 compressions/minute. Depth of at least 2 inches (5 cm) and less than 2.4 inches (6 cm) for adults and children
expectedActions.rationale: High-quality compressions are the primary determinant of survival in cardiac arrest.

expectedActions.shortAction: Defibrillate per Zoll biphasic setting (120 J first shock) for shockable VT
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Defibrillation dosing should follow manufacturer's recommendation in the case of biphasic defibrillators. Zoll — Adult – 120 J, 150 J, 200 J
expectedActions.rationale: Prompt defibrillation is essential for shockable rhythms in cardiac arrest.

expectedActions.shortAction: Give epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO during the first or second round of compressions
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If feasible, IV or IO access should be obtained. Administer Epinephrine 1mg during the first or second round of compressions.
expectedActions.rationale: Early epinephrine supports coronary perfusion pressure during resuscitation.
